title: Chapter test: Async Programming
summary: Ten questions on futures, executors, async concurrency and pinning. You need 70% to pass; you can retry and your best score is kept.

questions.explanation: The future is created but never polled.

questions.q: What type does `async fn total() -> u32` return when called?
questions.explanation: The body runs when the future is polled.

questions.q: Which crate provides a widely used async runtime?
questions.explanation: Others include async-std, smol and embassy.

questions.q: `a.await; b.await;` takes 3 s + 2 s. About how long does `join(a, b).await` take, if both just wait?
questions.explanation: The waits overlap; the longest one decides.

questions.q: How is a timeout usually built?
options: Racing the future against a sleep and dropping the loser

questions.q: Why is `std::thread::sleep` inside an async task a problem?
options: It blocks the executor thread, so no other task on it can run

questions.q: What does a minimal `block_on` do when poll returns Pending?
options: Parks the thread until the waker unparks it

questions.q: Which is the right way to hold a non-Unpin future in a struct and poll it?
questions.explanation: It must stay at one address.
